title: Token-throttle synthetic-mix harness for continuous-batching + queueing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create and validate a deterministic synthetic-load harness that combines continuous batching and queueing effects under mixed request profiles (short chat, long generation, embedding, reranking). Purpose is to measure tokens/sec throughput, p95 latency under realistic arrival skew, and to add automated regression detection to CI for changes in batching/kernel scheduling code.
hypothesis: When arrival skew and session stickiness are introduced alongside mixed payload sizes, continuous batching will produce non-linear amplification in p95 tail latency; token-level throughput gains from batching will be offset by queueing amplification for high-priority short requests unless preemptive routing or slot reservations are applied.
test_plan: 1) Implement synthetic client that can drive multiple arrival processes in parallel: Poisson for background embeddings, bursty ON/OFF for chat sessions, periodic large generations. 2) Add session stickiness and KV-cache warmup behavior for a fraction of traffic. 3) Run grid over arrival mixes, concurrency levels, and batching window sizes. 4) Collect token throughput, token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue length distribution, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rates. 5) Use regression detector (EWMA+ADWIN) to flag significant shifts vs baseline. 6) Store traces and flamegraphs for runs that exceed thresholds.
harness_config:
- clients: 128 synthetic clients across 4 arrival profiles
- profiles: [chat-short(60 tokens), chat-long(800 tokens), generation(2048 tokens), embedding(768 dims)]
- arrival_patterns: [poisson(lambda=2 r/s), burst(lambda=30 r/s, burst_duration=5s, idle=60s), periodic(1 every 10s)]
- session_stickiness: 30% of chat sessions are sticky with warm KV cache
- batching_window_ms: sweep [0, 5, 10, 25, 50]
- concurrency_sweep: [16, 32, 64, 128]
analysis_methodology: Aggregate per-run metrics into time-series (1s granularity). Compute rolling p95 over 30s windows and compare against baseline run at same configuration. Use ADWIN to detect sustained shifts in p95 and tokens/sec; complement with bootstrap resampling to estimate confidence intervals. For runs with flagged regressions, pull individual request traces and correlate batch composition (mix of short/long) with latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline run reproduces historical token/sec within ±5% for given hw profile
Regression detector triggers <2 false positives on 20 historical stable runs
Harness can run end-to-end and produce artifacts (csv + traces) within 90 minutes for full sweep
Documented runbook for running the harness and interpreting alerts exists in Confluence
